identity.title: REGENT: A Retrieval-Augmented Generalist Agent That Can Act In-Context in New Environments

problem.claim: The paper addresses rapid adaptation of generalist agents to new digital, robotic, and game-playing environments.

contributions.claim: A retrieval-augmented, semi-parametric agent, REGENT, trains a transformer policy on query and retrieved-neighbor sequences for finetuning-free in-context adaptation.

The authors report generalization to unseen robotics and game-playing environments with up to 3× fewer parameters and an order of magnitude fewer pre-training datapoints than current generalist agents.
The authors identify a simple retrieval-based 1-nearest-neighbor agent as a strong baseline for contemporary generalist agents.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present pre-training relatively small policies on relatively small datasets, then adapting them to unseen environments through retrieval-biased in-context learning without finetuning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that a simple retrieval-based 1-nearest-neighbor agent is surprisingly strong against current state-of-the-art generalist agents.
The authors report that REGENT significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art generalist agents while using up to 3× fewer parameters and up to 10× fewer pre-training datapoints.
The authors report generalization to unseen robotics and game-playing environments via retrieval augmentation and in-context learning.

narrative_sequence.summary: Rapid adaptation to new environments is framed as a deployment challenge for generalist agents.
The paper questions whether scaling existing agent architectures is the most effective route to generality.
It proposes small-policy pre-training followed by finetuning-free in-context adaptation, using retrieval as a bias for fast adaptation.
Starting from a strong nearest-neighbor baseline, the authors construct REGENT as a transformer policy over queries and retrieved neighbors.
REGENT is reported to generalize across unseen robotics and game-playing environments with reduced model and data requirements and higher performance than current generalist agents.

source_observation.claim: The abstract introduces a simple retrieval-based 1-nearest-neighbor agent before presenting the more complex REGENT system.

lessons.interpretation: A strong simple baseline can clarify whether added architectural complexity contributes beyond retrieval itself.
lessons.application: When proposing a sophisticated adaptive agent, establish a retrieval-only baseline first and state the incremental role of the learned policy.
lessons.exception: This is less suitable when a retrieval-only comparator cannot represent the task or violates the deployment setting.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs adaptation claims with resource comparisons, reporting parameter and pre-training-data reductions alongside performance comparisons.

lessons.interpretation: Aligning capability claims with efficiency quantities makes the claimed tradeoff more concrete.
lessons.application: Report performance and resource usage together when arguing that a smaller adaptive system is competitive or superior.
lessons.exception: Resource comparisons may mislead when training budgets, environments, or evaluation conditions are not matched.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify benchmark tasks, dataset sizes, evaluation metrics, comparator identities, or statistical uncertainty.
The conditions behind the reported 3× parameter and order-of-magnitude data reductions are unspecified.
